text:
## Description

A Python 3 program reads the initial grid, Takahashi’s starting cell, and the changes from standard input. After each move and update, it prints the sum of the products along all paths from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell, modulo 998244353.

## Preconditions

- **PRE-1 (Unverified)** — The grid dimensions are integers from 2 through 200000, with at most 200000 cells in total. The input supplies one integer from 0 through 998244352 for each cell, in row order.
- **PRE-2 (Unverified)** — The change count \(Q\) is an integer from 1 through 200000. The starting row and column are integers identifying a cell in the grid, using 1-based coordinates.
- **PRE-3 (Unverified)** — The input supplies \(Q\) changes in the stated format. Each change gives a direction of L, R, U, or D and an integer replacement value from 0 through 998244352. Every move stays within the grid when applied in input order.

## Postconditions

- **POST-1 (Unverified)** — Each change moves Takahashi one cell from his current position in the specified direction and replaces the destination’s value. Every other cell retains its value. Later changes use the resulting position and grid, including when a cell is revisited.
- **POST-2 (Unverified)** — After each change, each distinct path of \(H+W-1\) cells from \((1,1)\) to \((H,W)\) that moves only down or right contributes exactly once. Its contribution is the product of the current values of all its cells, including both endpoints. Paths with equal products contribute separately. A zero-valued cell makes every path through it contribute zero.
- **POST-3 (Unverified)** — Standard output contains exactly \(Q\) lines in change order. Line \(i\) contains the integer remainder from 0 through 998244352 of the sum in POST-2 after change \(i\).

## Test suggestions

- On a \(2\times2\) grid, use one legal move to update an endpoint. Check both path products and the single output line (PRE-1–PRE-3, POST-1–POST-3).
- Revisit a cell, first setting it to zero and later restoring a nonzero value. Check which path contributions disappear and return in order (PRE-3, POST-1–POST-3).
- Set every cell to 998244352 on a \(2\times3\) grid and perform a legal same-value update. Check that all three equal products contribute and the answer is 3 (POST-1–POST-3).

## Unspecified behavior

Handling of malformed input, out-of-range values, and moves that leave the grid is unspecified.
